title: Choose Edges to Maximize Score in a Tree
summary: Given a weighted tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where the root is at node 0 and edges are defined by a 2D array, select edges such that no two are adjacent to maximize the sum of their weights.
statement: Given a weighted tree with n nodes numbered 0 to n-1, where the root is at node 0 and edges are defined by a 2D array, select edges such that no two are adjacent to maximize the sum of their weights. Return the maximum possible sum. You can choose no edges, resulting in a sum of 0. Two edges are adjacent if they share a common node.
constraints: edges[i]=[parent,weight] describes the rooted weighted edge to node i; edges[0]=[-1,-1].
Choose edges sharing no endpoint; choosing none is allowed.
Return the maximum possible weight sum, even when some weights are negative.
hints: For each node, compare states where its parent edge is unavailable versus may be chosen.
Without choosing a child edge, add each child’s unrestricted optimum; choosing one child edge switches that child to its blocked state.
Compute the baseline and the best single child-edge improvement.
A matching can use at most one edge incident to the current node, so these states enumerate every local possibility and independent child subtrees add.
